newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Buoyant markets turn McIntosh around.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Buoyant markets turn McIntosh around.

text.p: Stockbroker McIntosh Securties Ltd said the turnaround in net profit for the year ended June 30 reflected buoyant market conditions.

McIntosh, which is 19.9 percent owned by Dutch bank and insurance group Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING), reported a net profit of A$10.05 million for 1995/96, compared with a net loss of A$7.04 million a year earlier.

Managing director Bruce Parncutt said that while the Australian broking industry remained highly competitive, McIntosh's performance was pleasing given that it was able to produce a more satisfactory result for shareholders.

"We are looking to increase our market share in private client broking and have already made a number of moves designed to lift productivity and diversify our income base in this area," Parncutt said.
McIntosh shares closed steady at 72 cents on Thursday.
